To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ozonation of human HIV-infested plasmas may be a novel approach for developing a global HIV vaccine.

1) a global vaccine against HIV is feasible; 2) the vaccine will be prepared by pooling thousands of small HIV-infected plasmapheresis; 3) the plasmas will be sterilized and inactivated by ozone; 4) therapeutic albumin and ozonoethyle oleate will be added to the vaccine to increase its absorption and reactivity with the immune system; 5) a partner collaboration is essential for producing and testing the vaccine.

the ozone treatment of human plasma from HIV-infected patients may produce a vaccine able to generate a proper neutralizing antibody response and a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte response, thus able to fight the HIV pandemics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a novel vaccine for HIV infection.
a new approach for developing a vaccine against HIV.

the development and the preliminary testing, in a partner collaboration, of an innovative vaccine able to counteract the HIV diversity and mutability, and the need of a partner cooperation for the production and the testing of the vaccine in humans is of paramount importance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ozonation of HIV-infected human plasmas for preparing a global anti-HIV vaccine is feasible and promising.
the HIV-infected patients may contribute to the fight against HIV pandemia by donating a small quantity of their plasmas for preparing the global vaccine.

the HIV-infected human plasmas, when treated with ozone, can be used for producing a global HIV vaccine able to generate a proper neutralization of HIV and to stimulate a cytotoxic T lymphocytes response against HIV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-patients could help fight the HIV pandemic by donating their plasmas for preparing an effective vaccine.
HIV patients may help fight the pandemic.
HIV-infected patients, who are in need of an efficacious vaccine for their own health, may also help to produce the best vaccine able to counteract the HIV pandemic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ozonated plasma may be considered as a novel source of antigens for preparing a global HIV vaccine.
a vaccine against HIV may be produced with the help of HIV-infected human plasmas.
HIV-patients, who are in the front line in the fight against HIV, may help fight the pandemia by contributing to the development of an efficacious vaccine.
